commentary: The portfolio is entirely in cash and stays there today. This run was triggered automatically because two names I said I wanted to buy at certain prices got close to those prices — but when I checked the live market rather than yesterday's closing prices, neither one actually met the conditions I wrote down. Palo Alto is trading below the level I said I needed it to reclaim, and it reports earnings on August 18; AbbVie reports on July 31, and I had explicitly said I would wait until after that report. Changing my mind ten days early because a stock drifted near a number would be abandoning my own process for no new information. Travelers is the most interesting business I own no shares of — it just reported profit nearly double what analysts expected, trades at twelve times earnings, and has no earnings report for three months — but it sits within one percent of its all-time high, right on top of a large price gap, and any sensible protective stop would sit somewhere an ordinary week could reach. That is a good company at a bad entry price, so it goes on the list with a level, not into the book. Meanwhile the market's recent leaders are being sold hard even as the index holds up, which automatically halves how much I am allowed to risk and is a poor backdrop for buying anything that has already run. I would change my mind on a Travelers pullback to the mid-350s that holds, or on a genuinely constructive reaction to either of the earnings reports coming in the next ten days.
